verdict.rationale: Jev's docs have a dedicated cookbooks section covering real multi-step tasks: LLM guardrail screening with pass/review/block routing, hierarchical classification via beam search, reranking with measured accuracy gains, and citation checking. Separate pattern guides (intent routing, composite scoring, fan-out) go well beyond single-call snippets. Missing for 10: evidence of full runnable code walkthroughs showing each cookbook's depth and how to adapt it, and independent or hands-on corroboration that developers have successfully adapted these cookbooks.

support.subject: As a developer, official cookbooks or worked examples show real end-to-end tasks — not just single-call snippets — that I can adapt

citations.quote: Screen every message going into and out of an LLM app with one TypeSafe request, thresholding hazard probabilities and severity to pass, review, block, or route.
Classifies documents through deep patent, retail product, biomedical, and source-code hierarchies using parallel beam search over TypeSafe Choice probabilities.
uses one TypeSafe question per query-candidate pair to raise top-1 accuracy from 5% to 18% and top-10 accuracy from 38% to 62%.
Catch wrong or hallucinated citations by checking against the source document.
Classify incoming requests and route each to the optimal handler: deterministic logic, a specialist LLM, or a human.
